title: Cyber Defenders Unit 3 · Private means private (6-8)

items.q: A game offers a free badge if you share your school name and birthday. What is the best way to price this trade?
choices: Share both: a free badge is always worth it
Weigh the small benefit against facts that point at you, and keep them
Share your birthday only if the badge is rare
Ask a friend to share their facts instead

items.q: A fun quiz asks for your pet's name, your birth month and the street you live on. What are those questions really doing?
choices: Guessing your nickname from your favorite color
Making the quiz harder so it feels like a real test
Harvesting facts that can point at you or help unlock accounts
Checking that you are old enough to play

items.q: You shared too much in a post last night. What is true about fixing it?
choices: You can delete it and ask for help, but copies may still exist
Deleting it erases every copy everywhere at once
Nothing at all can be done, so there is no point trying
Posting lots more will bury it forever

items.q: A service quietly saves your game scores and the places you play from. Who wrote that part of your footprint?
choices: You did, in a post you wrote
A friend did, by tagging you
The service did, by collecting data about you
Nobody: scores and places leave no trail

items.q: Why is deleting a post not the same as erasing it?
choices: Copies and screenshots can live on after your copy is gone
Deleted posts always come back the next day
Only a trusted adult is allowed to press delete
Deleting only works on posts with pictures

items.q: Years from now, a school reads your old post teasing a classmate. How will it most likely read that post?
choices: As a joke that says nothing about you
As part of your reputation, shaping what it thinks of you
As proof that someone else used your account
It cannot: old posts vanish after a year

items.q: A message says: this is your coach, hurry, send the mailbox key now or the team loses its place. Which levers is it pulling?
choices: Kindness and fear only
Authority and urgency
No levers: it sounds like a normal message
Research and a recipe

items.q: A trickster knows your name, your school and the route you walk home. Where did those facts most likely come from?
choices: Facts already shared in public, like posts and profiles
A locked mailbox that was broken open
Pure guessing: nobody could ever know all three
A trusted adult who handed them over

items.q: A friendly message asks you to confirm a private fact right away. What is the move that defeats the trick?
choices: Reply fast, before the deadline in the message passes
Ask another friend in the same chat to confirm it
Verify through a different channel, like asking the person in real life
Send half the fact and see what happens
